analysis.title: Eat Until 80% Full: Nearing a Tactical Bottom, but Breadth Inconsistent with Final Low
key_insights: BTIG technical strategy says the downside is tactically about 80% done with S&P futures near 7100, the top of its targeted 7k-7100 range. It expects a short-term bottom in the next few days around SPX 7k.

After a relief rally, BTIG expects a more broad-based breadth washout is needed before a final low. It has no downside SPX objective for that yet. The three prior occurrences with a similar set-up had significant downside risk ahead.

Short-term capitulation signals: the SPX Daily Sentiment Index closed at 10, the lowest since the April 2025 Liberation Day lows. The VIX futures curve inverted by over 6 points, the most since spring 2025.
From SPX around 7k, BTIG sees a 4-5% bounce that would take the index back toward the 200 DMA at 7348.

Breadth argues against a final low: 50% of SPX names are still above their 50 DMAs. In SPX pullbacks of 8% or more over the last 30 years, the median share above the 50 DMA was 11% and the highest was 44% (Aug 2024), then 25%.

Apple is near all-time highs. At SPX bottoms since 2015 the closest AAPL was to its 52-week high was -11.8% (Aug 2024), with a median of -23%. BTIG says a final low with AAPL this close to its high would be unprecedented and sees downside risk ahead for AAPL as part of a bigger washout.

market_movers.rationale: BTIG (Not Rated) sees downside risk for AAPL because it remains near all-time highs, which it says is inconsistent with a final market low.

risk_factors: Breadth has not washed out, so a bounce from SPX 7k may be followed by a lower final low.
Three prior occurrences with a similar set-up had significant downside risk ahead.
AAPL near all-time highs implies further downside risk for the stock and the market.
